messages.content: How is the air quality in Los Angeles right now?

function.name: plant_biomass
function.description: Calculate the biomass of a plant species in a given area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species_name.description: The name of the plant species.

area.description: The area of the forest in square kilometers. This is a float type value.

density.description: The density of the plant species in the area. Default is average global density. This is a float type value.

message.content:
I don’t have access to live sensor feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact PM₂.₅ or ozone levels at this very moment.  
For up‑to‑date information you can check:

| Source | What it offers |
|--------|----------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Real‑time readings from EPA‑approved monitoring stations across California, plus forecasted values. |
| **AQICN** (aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/) | Global network with local station data, health advisories, and historical trends. |
| **Weather apps / Google “LA air quality”** | Many weather services display an AQI index based on recent measurements. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, just search “Los Angeles air quality” in your browser—most results will pull directly from one of those sources.
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in LA. We cannot provide real-time data; we should explain limitation and suggest resources like AirNow or AQICN. No tool needed.
